thread:
sam.k: Heads-up — multiple embedded-sdk customers reporting streaming sessions aborted mid-response. Billing shows these as 5xx. Example request-id: req_8a3f2c. Seen across regions. Any quick triage? :eyes:
ingrid: Can you paste the raw server-side logs for one of the failures and the client call you used to reproduce? Also want the gateway trace id if available.

mike: If these are actual client disconnects we often see ECONNRESET / broken pipe. We used to classify some of those as gateway 5xx when the proxy fails to flush trailers. Might be that.
sam.k: Pasting a trimmed trace and a curl we used for repro:

```
# client
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open","prompt":"stream test"}' 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/respond
```

logs (gateway):
```
2026-02-12T14:22:11.123Z gateway[proxy-3] INFO request=req_8a3f2c start
2026-02-12T14:22:21.456Z backend[serving-45] INFO open stream, sent headers
2026-02-12T14:22:22.789Z gateway[proxy-3] ERROR write failed: broken pipe (EPIPE) request=req_8a3f2c trace=tr_0b9c
2026-02-12T14:22:22.790Z gateway[proxy-3] INFO request=req_8a3f2c ended status=500
```

sre-oncall: That pattern (proxy EPIPE -> end as 500) is exactly what flags the billing pipeline. Historically we didn't have a reliable signal to differentiate client-initiated abort vs gateway failure.
ingrid: Do we have the client-side behavior? If embedded-sdk is closing streams early on some network conditions it should be counted as client abort not 5xx.
sam.k: Repro snippet from the SDK (node):
```
const r = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${key}` } });
const reader = r.body.getReader();
// artificially abort after ~2s to mimic the customer's flakey connectivity
setTimeout(() => { reader.cancel(); }, 2000);
```

mike: That cancel looks like a clean client-side abort. If the SDK closes before we write trailers the proxy throws EPIPE when it writes.

eng-runtime: We need to change the classification heuristics: if we see EPIPE/ECONNRESET within X ms after client FIN and the backend stream had already emitted tokens, mark as client_abort instead of gateway_5xx. Will need a small change in gateway and update billing tagger.

ops-bot: Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/stream-errors?var=req=req_8a3f2c (captures traces and per-route ratios)

ingrid: Short-term mitigation: can we add a metric filter that excludes EPIPEs from billing for streaming routes for the next 24–48h while we validate? Also ask support to share probe samples from impacted customers so we can confirm. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

eng-runtime: I'll cut a canary patch to the proxy today that relaxes the 5xx rule for obvious client-closes (detect by `tcp_fin_seen` flag + EPIPE). Will roll to 10% and monitor error-rate and revenue metrics. If safe, promote.
mike: Also add a logging flag to capture the socket-level event so we have evidence for support/billing.
sam.k: Awesome — sending a list of 6 affected customer request ids and sample SDK versions in a follow-up DM. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: Filed ENG-1279 to track the fix and billing-rule change. Will follow up on pager if the canary spikes.

ingrid: Please keep me looped; need to update customers with a non-actionable explanation while we fix classification.

sam.k: Will draft a customer-facing note and post here for review before sending.
